q: What does it mean that the heat of combustion of diesel is about $43\,\text{MJ/kg}$?
a: About $43\,\text{MJ}$ of energy is released when one kilogram of diesel burns. The heat of combustion is energy per unit of mass.

q: How much energy is released when $5.0\,\text{kg}$ of air-dried firewood ($H = 15\,\text{MJ/kg}$) is burnt?
A package says: energy $1500\,\text{kJ}$ per hundred grams. What is the energy content of the food in $\text{MJ/kg}$, and why is it the same thing as the heat of combustion?
a: $1500\,\text{kJ} = 1500 \cdot (1 : 1000)\,\text{MJ} = 1.5\,\text{MJ}$ and $100\,\text{g} = 100 \cdot (1 : 1000)\,\text{kg} = 0.100\,\text{kg}$, so the energy content is $1.5\,\text{MJ} : 0.100\,\text{kg} = 15\,\text{MJ/kg}$. It is energy per unit of mass, like the heat of combustion.
